 Use the tenant registry's exact dimension keys and source attributes; the example requires a `material` dimension reading `material`. Filters require every dimension to match and allow any listed value within one dimension, with trimmed case-insensitive exact value matching. Unknown or duplicate dimensions are rejected. A configured derived price band uses that registry's numeric source and cuts; there is no separate numeric-price, currency or gift policy here. Only explicit `inStock: true` is eligible. Availability and attributes are commerce-feed assertions, not an inventory or catalog-ownership check. The first trimmed ID wins before filtering; a later duplicate cannot restore an excluded item. No matches returns an empty result without relaxing filters.
 
 The strict body accepts only `userId`, optional `sessionId`, `surface`, `consent`, `weights`, `limit`, and required `candidates`/`intent`. IDs are nonempty trimmed strings up to 200 characters; every candidate requires boolean `inStock`, with flat string/finite-number/boolean/null/string-array attributes. Maximums: 500 candidates, 16 filters, 8 values per filter, 64 characters per dimension, 128 per value, and 256 KiB of actual UTF-8 JSON. `limit` is an integer from 1 to 500, default 9, applied after ranking. Optional `weights.affinity` and `weights.dims` values must be finite numbers from 0 to 10; zero affinity preserves eligible feed order. Caller-supplied affinity or query fields are rejected.
 
-Success includes `source: "structured-intent"`, `tenant`, `configVersion`, `order`, and `items` with `id`, original zero-based `feedRank`, result `rank`, `score` and affinity `drivers`. `inputCount = dropped + filteredCount + eligibleCount`: `dropped` counts duplicate IDs, `filteredCount` counts unique first records rejected by stock or filters, and `eligibleCount` is before the limit; `order.length` is the returned count. Stored, cookie or body refusal removes private affinity influence and drivers. Ranking creates no behavioral profile or visit; necessary refusal preferences may be persisted. Responses are `no-store`; invalid input/filter is 400, ownership refusal 401, oversized body 413, and configuration/internal unavailability 503. This endpoint does not persist product decisions or establish customer/SFCC acceptance. The separate `POST /sort` candidate-preserving contract is unchanged.
+Success includes `source: "structured-intent"`, `tenant`, `configVersion`, `order`, and `items` with `id`, original zero-based `feedRank`, result `rank`, `score` and affinity `drivers`. `inputCount = dropped + filteredCount + eligibleCount`: `dropped` counts duplicate IDs, `filteredCount` counts unique first records rejected by stock or filters, and `eligibleCount` is before the limit; `order.length` is the returned count. Stored, cookie or body refusal removes private affinity influence and drivers. Ranking creates no behavioral profile or visit; necessary refusal preferences may be persisted. Responses are `no-store`; invalid input/filter is 400, ownership refusal 401, oversized body 413, and configuration/internal unavailability 503. Customer/SFCC acceptance remains separate. `POST /sort` retains its candidate-preserving ranking behavior.
 
+Both product-sort endpoints add `persistence: { "status": "scheduled", "recordId": "…" }` when a background R2 write is registered. This is best effort and does not confirm storage. Otherwise they return `{ "status": "not_scheduled", "reason": "tracking_refused" | "storage_unavailable" | "context_unavailable" | "invalid_record" | "record_too_large" }`; the ranking response still succeeds. Tracking refusal schedules no capture; personalization refusal with tracking allowed can record the default order and empty private drivers.
+
+The separate `product-sort` stream stores a strict version-1 whole-request record: `record_id` and random `request_id`, signed `tenant`/`visitor_id`/`session_id`, request `ts` from before profile resolution, `configVersion`, `mode` (`sort` or `intent`), effective `consent`, applied `weights` and `affinityWeight`, exact returned `order`/`items`, `inputCount`/`dropped`/`filteredCount`/`eligibleCount`/`returnedCount`, and `limit`/normalized explicit `intent` filters (both null for plain sort). It excludes raw candidates, the full profile, request headers and network metadata. Each request uses its own UUID-named object under `{tenant}/{date}/{hour}/product-sort/`; the complete UTF-8 NDJSON record is limited to 1 MiB with no truncation. It is a ranking receipt, not a rendered exposure, and feeds no content learning statistics.
+
+Read a completed receipt with operator-authorized `GET /v1/{tenant}/ledger/{record_id}?stream=product-sort`; list its export objects with `GET /v1/{tenant}/ledger/batches?date=YYYY-MM-DD&stream=product-sort`. Default batch exports retain their legacy streams and exclude product sort. Readers and export consumers must apply the existing erasure cutoffs; the existing rewrite removes matching visitor/time rows. Background failures, process termination and erasure suppression can leave a scheduled ID unreadable. No durable acknowledgement, retry or every-decision completeness is provided; the erasure check and write are not atomic, and one object per request adds listing/rewrite cost. Scheduled warehouse delivery and full §1.6 acceptance remain open.
+
 ### `GET /v1/{tenant}/decisions/snapshot?page=home&visitorId=<id>[&brand=<brand>][&channel=<channel>]`
 
 Every slot's decision for the page, in page order, and the record of each. Site key.

 | `GET learn/exploring?slot=&brand=[&limit=][&cursor=]` | The pieces under the slot's observation floor, least observed first, one page at a time, with the slot's exploration mode, share and floor: what exploration serves on purpose |
 | `GET learn/queue?brand=` | What needs a person, as counts: proposals pending, slots that have learned nothing yet, slots whose trust dial is above zero, pieces frozen or rejected, erasures still to be rewritten. The landing page of an operator application. Operator token |
 | `GET visitors/{visitorId}/receipts[?limit=&cursor=]` | What this shopper was served, newest first, each with the sentences that say why: the interest matched, the region's trend, your model's term, the journey-stage, freshness, fatigue, merchandising and diversity rules, the learned lift and whether it was applied, a pin, the holdout arm, an explored pick. An erased shopper answers 410. Operator token |
 | `GET visitors/{visitorId}/recent` | The visitor's ring of recent decisions, what attribution reads |
-| `GET ledger/{decision_id}` and `GET ledger/{outcome_id}?stream=outcome` | One record from the ledger by id, no index needed; behind by the queue's lag during a peak |
-| `GET ledger/batches?date=YYYY-MM-DD[&stream=decision\|outcome][&cursor=]` | The day's batch objects, so a warehouse job knows what to fetch with its own storage credentials. The partitions are the export |
+| `GET ledger/{decision_id}`, `GET ledger/{outcome_id}?stream=outcome`, and `GET ledger/{record_id}?stream=product-sort` | One record from the ledger by id, no index needed; content/outcomes can lag their queue, while product-sort capture is best effort |
+| `GET ledger/batches?date=YYYY-MM-DD[&stream=decision\|outcome\|product-sort][&cursor=]` | The day's batch objects, so a warehouse job knows what to fetch with its own storage credentials. Product-sort objects require the explicit selector; apply erasure cutoffs when loading |
 | `GET ledger/erasures` | The visitors whose erasure is pending, each with the moment of erasure: a warehouse job drops their rows at or before that moment from what it loads, until the nightly rewrite has removed them from the objects themselves. `ledger/batches` says how many are pending |
 | `POST ledger/erasures` `{ visitorId }` | The ledger half of an erasure: writes the tombstone every reader honours at once and empties the visitor's ring. The identity erase route calls the same function after erasing the profile. `POST ledger/erasures/rewrite` runs the nightly rewrite now |
 | `GET replay/{decision_id}` | Decides again from the documents at the recorded revisions, the archived snapshot and the record's inputs, and compares field by field: `{ equal, diff[], used }` |
 | `POST learn/report` `{ date, brand?, policies? }` and `GET learn/report?date=&brand=` | The day under the learning policy and the reporting overlays side by side, the holdout arms, the realized exploration share. The day is the sum of its hours: five minutes after an hour closes the platform folds its ledger objects into one aggregate, so a day of any size answers, and `GET` for today answers through the last closed hour. `hours` says which hours are in (`built`), which closed hours are not yet (`missing`), and how far back the batch ring reaches when it credits an outcome (`horizonMs`, two days). Custom `policies` are computed over the records themselves and answer 413 past 800 ledger objects in the day; the built-in overlays never do. No visitor id in the result |
